Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the model forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the data across all 5 examples, I need to find patterns in the differences between:
1. Model forecasts (30-day horizon)
2. True outcomes (30-day horizon)

Let me analyze the differences:

## Example 1 (2025-10-30)
History is around 78-79 range, slowly drifting up
Model forecasts are generally lower than true outcomes
Looking at the first few days:
- Day 1: Model 78.70 vs True 78.67 (off by +0.03)
- Day 5: Model 81.26 vs True 81.49 (off by +0.23)
- Day 10: Model 80.28 vs True 81.34 (off by +1.06)
- Day 15: Model 79.78 vs True 81.36 (off by +1.58)
- Day 20: Model 80.47 vs True 82.21 (off by +1.74)
- Day 25: Model 81.15 vs True 82.43 (off by +1.28)
- Day 30: Model 81.95 vs True 82.85 (off by +0.90)

The model appears to be under-predicting, especially as we get further into the 30-day horizon.

## Example 2 (2025-10-29)
Very similar pattern:
- Day 4: Model 78.52 vs True 78.54 (close)
- Day 5: Model 81.09 vs True 81.20 (off by +0.11)
- Day 10: Model 80.40 vs True 80.65 (off by +0.25)
- Day 15: Model 79.69 vs True 80.66 (off by +1.00)


- Day 20: Model 80.87 vs True 81.68 (off by +0.81)
- Day 25: Model 81.23 vs True 81.82 (off by +0.59)
- Day 30: Model 79.08 vs True 82.85 (off by +3.77)

I notice a consistent pattern of the model underestimating future prices, with discrepancies growing more pronounced as we look further into the 30-day horizon. The differences aren't uniform, but there
